data.title: 3M CEO sees innovation, data centers, cost cuts extending turnaround
data.description:
3M (MMM) Chairman and Chief Executive William Brown said the industrial conglomerate is exceeding key turnaround targets as stronger execution, new products and portfolio changes support growth and margin expansion.

Speaking Tuesday at the Morgan Stanley 14th Annual Laguna Conference, Brown said 3M (MMM) is tracking ahead of the goals outlined at its 2025 investor day. The company has improved product availability, accelerated innovation and created a more accountable operating culture during his first two and a half years as CEO.

“We are clearly making progress,” Brown said. “We’re seeing more sustained organic growth. We’re seeing a clear step up in margins.”

For investors, the operational turnaround is an important next chapter for 3M (MMM) after years of uncertainty tied to costly litigation. The company has worked to move beyond multibillion-dollar settlements involving PFAS, commonly called “forever chemicals,” and allegedly defective military earplugs used by soldiers in combat. With much of that legal exposure better defined, investor attention has increasingly shifted toward growth, cash generation and the potential for higher margins.

Service levels improve

One of Brown’s initial priorities was improving on-time and complete deliveries, known as OTIF. That measure has risen from the low 80% range to about 90%, while parts of the consumer business are consistently reaching the mid-90% range.

Brown said delivery problems are no longer a major concern in most discussions with distributors. The next objective is to increase service levels while reducing inventory and shortening lead times.

“If you do all those three together, that’s what we’re trying to do,” he said.

Better service has also helped reduce customer attrition. 3M (MMM) is using artificial intelligence tools to identify customers that may be considering switching suppliers, giving sales teams an opportunity to respond before the business is lost.

Product launches accelerate

3M (MMM) has directed about 80% of its research and development spending toward priority markets where its materials-science capabilities can provide a competitive advantage. Those markets include semiconductors, data centers, aerospace and defense.

The company launched about 125 products three years ago, compared with 284 last year. Brown expects more than 350 launches this year.

New products accounted for roughly 11% of sales when Brown arrived. That figure has risen into the mid-teens and is expected to reach about 20% by the end of 2027. Historically, the measure was closer to 25%.

Brown said 3M expects to generate roughly $400 million of growth above its underlying markets this year, with more than half coming from innovation. The contribution from new products should increase further in 2027.

Microsoft partnership supports data-center push

Brown highlighted expanded beam optical technology as one of 3M’s (MMM) most promising data-center opportunities. The system provides durable, dust-resistant fiber connections that can reduce installation costs by as much as 85%, according to the company.

Microsoft (MSFT) has adopted the technology as a standard for its data centers. Five other global hyperscale operators are conducting qualification work or proof-of-concept testing, Brown said.

3M has (MMM) about 50 patents covering the technology and another 50 pending. Still, Brown said widespread adoption will require licensing, contract manufacturing and common industry standards. A group formed around the technology now includes 44 companies.

3M (MMM) plans to double its internal manufacturing capacity for expanded beam optics this year. Brown estimated that the addressable market could approach $2 billion within the next year or two.

The company’s broader data-center business generated about $600 million in revenue last year. Its products include optical and copper connections, cable terminations, splicing materials and heat-resistant ceramic fibers.

Brown said 3M (MMM) has room to gain share even if the pace of overall data-center construction slows.

Growth carries into second half

3M (MMM) posted organic growth of about 5.4% in the second quarter and 3.3% for the first half. Safety and Industrial grew more than 8%, while Transportation and Electronics expanded by nearly 6%.

Brown said the momentum has continued into the third quarter. The company expects full-year organic growth above 3.5%, implying faster growth in the second half than in the first.

Consumer electronics, automotive production and portions of the consumer-products market remain under pressure. However, Brown said point-of-sale trends for 3M’s consumer products have improved and retailer inventory reductions are beginning to normalize.

Pricing expected to offset oil costs

Higher oil prices are expected to add between $150 million and $175 million to 3M’s (MMM) costs this year, up from an earlier estimate of $125 million.

The company expects pricing increases to offset that expense on a dollar-for-dollar basis. Brown said price increases should average about 2% in the second half and 1.5% for the full year.

The increases may create a margin headwind of 10 to 20 basis points, although Brown said they should prevent the higher oil costs from reducing earnings.

Factory reductions offer longer-term runway

3M also is shrinking its manufacturing network as it shifts from a decentralized holding-company structure toward a more integrated operating model.

The company ended last year with 110 factories and 84 distribution centers. Its factory count has since fallen below 100, with additional closures or consolidations under consideration.

Brown described the manufacturing overhaul as a three- to five-year effort. The company also sees savings opportunities in information technology, human resources, finance and other administrative functions.

3M is tracking toward an operating margin above 25% by 2027. Brown said factory consolidation and lower structural costs should provide additional margin expansion beyond that target.

“The opportunities ahead of us are more than I thought coming in,” Brown said. “They’re greater than we’ve seen to date.”

data.title: Skyworks Solutions surges 13%, rebounding from the previous day
data.description:
Shares of Skyworks Solutions (SWKS), an analog and mixed-signal semiconductor company, jumped nearly 13% on Tuesday, rebounding sharply after a roughly 10% pullback the previous session. The advance came amid fresh coverage reporting that the company's proposed merger with Qorvo had entered its final stages, with U.S. antitrust review completed and only China's regulatory approval remaining.

The stock closed at $89.33, up $10.07 from its prior close.

data.title: 3 things to look out for on Wednesday
data.description:
Wall Street’s major market averages concluded lower on Tuesday as investors prepared for the Federal Reserve’s interest rate decision.

The blue-chip Dow (DJI) closed -0.6%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) lost -0.4%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) finished -0.7%.

Now, here are three things to look out for on Wednesday:

  • The Fed will announce its policy decision, with federal funds futures trading implying a more than 90% probability of a 25-point rate increase.
  • The August retail sales report will be released by the U.S. Census Bureau. The headline number is expected to rise 0.8% M/M, accelerating from the prior month's 0.6% decrease.
  • Salesforce (CRM) will hold an Investor & Analyst Session at its Dreamforce event. The stock has surged nearly 35% from a month ago.

data.title: Wall Street closed in the red ahead of the upcoming FOMC rate decision
data.description:
Wall Street’s major market averages concluded lower on Tuesday as investors awaited the Federal Reserve’s interest rate decision on Wednesday.

The blue-chip Dow (DJI) closed -0.6%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) lost -0.4%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) finished -0.7%.

From a sector-by-sector vantage point, nine of the 11 segments finished in the red and were led lower by consumer discretionary. At the other end of the spectrum, energy was the strongest performer as oil (CL1:COM) advanced. 

The bond-market selloff adds pressure ahead of the Federal Reserve's interest-rate decision Wednesday, with investors expecting officials to raise short-term borrowing costs for the first time since July 2023.

“Market consensus is for a 25-basis-point rate hike when the FOMC announces its decision tomorrow, September 16.  The ongoing, escalating, and spreading conflict in the Middle East is driving inflation higher. As the U.S. midterm elections approach, the September FOMC meeting is likely the central bank's last chance to raise the short-term Fed Funds Rate without being accused of political favoritism,” Seeking Alpha analyst Andrew Hecht stated.

The U.S. 2-Year Treasury yield (US2Y) held flat near 4.67%, the U.S. 10-Year Treasury yield (US10Y) ticked higher by 1 basis point to 5.00%, and the U.S. 30-Year Treasury yield (US30Y) pushed up 1 basis point to 5.36%. 

“The Federal Reserve has little choice but to hike rates on Wednesday, especially since the bond market has been signaling for weeks that higher rates are warranted, given warm inflation data, strong earnings and a sturdy labor market. The stock market would be disappointed if the Fed didn't hike rates on Wednesday,” Carol Schleif of BMO Wealth Management stated.

As for stocks that were on the move, shares of QUALCOMM (QCOM) ended +4.1%, while shares of Coinbase (COIN) closed -10%.

data.title: Texas regulator approves Exxon's $5B carbon capture project after lengthy battle
data.description:
ExxonMobil (XOM) has been granted permission to store carbon dioxide emissions in underground wells in Texas after state regulators narrowly approved its application on Tuesday, the Financial Times reported, paving the way for the company to advance a $5B-plus plan to build the world's largest carbon capture pipeline network.

The permit for the Rose carbon capture and storage project will enable Exxon (XOM) to inject ~53M metric tons of its clients' carbon emissions into three underground wells it has drilled at sites in Jefferson County, ~90 miles east of Houston.

Representatives on the Texas Railroad Commission voted two to one in favor of granting Exxon (XOM) the permit following a public hearing that reflected mounting public and political opposition to carbon capture and storage in Louisiana and Texas.

Exxon (XOM) Senior VP of CCS Dominic Genetti said the decision was a "major milestone" that allows the company to continue expanding its business across the U.S. Gulf Coast.

However, analysts say the Trump administration's decision earlier this week to roll back climate rules limiting greenhouse gas emissions from power plants could dent demand for CCS technology in the power sector.

data.title: Google releases new Gemini models built to improve conversing capabilities of voice agents
data.description:
Google (GOOG)(GOOGL) released a pair of new Gemini models on Tuesday, 3.8 Live and 3.8 Live Extended Thinking, which were designed to improve the capabilities of voice agents.

"For developers and enterprises, these models deliver the building blocks for reliable, production-ready voice agents," said Google engineer Tom Ouyang in a blog post. "They also make speaking with Gemini across the Gemini app, Google Workspace, and Search more fluid and collaborative—helping you tackle complex tasks using just your voice."

Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking scored an 82.6% on the Artificial Intelligence Speech to Speech Index. It just outperformed OpenAI's (OPENAI) GPT-Live-1 Astra, which scored an 81.5%, and SpaceXAI's (SPCX) Grok Voice Think Fast 2.0, which scored an 81.3%.

"For tasks that require deeper reasoning, 3.8 Live Extended Thinking reasons and speaks simultaneously," Ouyang said. "It delivers increased intelligence for complex workflows while maintaining an uninterrupted conversational flow—using early verbal cues like 'Let me check that…' to acknowledge prompts naturally, and live progress narration to walk users through multi-step background tasks as they progress."

Google is also partnering with Salesforce (CRM), Genspark and Lumeris on use cases for the new models.

"By bringing together real-time, multimodal capabilities with agentic AI, we're exploring new ways to create richer, more intuitive customer experiences from first contact to resolution," said Bob Van Osten, vice president of Product for Agentforce at Salesforce.

Gemini 3.8 Live is available today for developers in the Gemini API and Google AI Studio, in private preview in Gemini Enterprise and for all users in Search Live. Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking is available today for developers in the Gemini API and Google AI Studio, in private preview for enterprises in Gemini Enterprise and for all users in Gemini Live and Google AI Pro.

data.title: Middleby rises after J.P. Morgan upgrade cites earnings, margin potential
data.description:
Middleby (MIDD) shares climbed as much as 3.8% after J.P. Morgan upgraded the commercial cooking-equipment maker to Overweight from Neutral, citing the potential for stronger earnings and a higher valuation. The S&P 500 (SP500) was negative for the day.

Analyst Tami Zakaria said Middleby (MIDD) could benefit as management works to accelerate growth and improve profitability following the spinoff of Midera Food Processing.

Middleby’s stock had been under pressure since July. Zakaria attributed the decline partly to disappointing second-quarter margins. Some event-driven investors also reduced or closed their positions after the Midera separation.

Those factors may create an opportunity for longer-term investors. J.P. Morgan expects margins to recover during the coming quarters as price increases and cost reductions take effect.

The firm also sees relatively modest expectations for the second half of 2026. That could make it easier for Middleby to meet its forecasts or deliver better-than-anticipated results.

J.P. Morgan set a December 2027 price target of $147. Its previous target was $141 for December 2026. The new target represents about 34% upside from Middleby’s latest closing price.

Middleby on Sept. 9 reaffirmed its full-year forecast for adjusted earnings of $6.73 to $6.89 a share on revenue of $2.48 billion to $2.53 billion. The company also maintained third-quarter guidance for earnings of $1.67 to $1.83 a share and revenue of $620 million to $640 million.

For investors, the upgrade rests on the view that Middleby’s (MIDD) recent weakness reflects temporary margin pressure and post-spinoff selling rather than a lasting deterioration in its business. The main test will be whether pricing actions and cost savings produce the expected improvement while the streamlined company delivers on its 2026 guidance.

data.title: Hot money or structural shift? Inside the emerging market debt surge
data.description:
Emerging market (EEM) debt issuance is on track to break records for the second consecutive year, fueled by sustained economic growth, substantial refinancing requirements and a surge in investor demand for portfolio diversification, according to Stefan Weiler, head of CEEMEA Debt Capital Markets at J.P. Morgan.

Since 2022, when issuance totaled some $110B, volumes have climbed steadily each year, with 2026 poised to surpass last year's historic highs, Weiler told CNBC in an interview.

The current wave of capital flowing into emerging markets marks a notable departure from past boom-bust cycles. Unlike the hot-money dynamics that contributed to the late-1990s Asian financial crisis, today's inflows appear structural rather than opportunistic, Weiler contended.

Emerging markets have attracted net inflows for 16 consecutive months—excluding a brief disruption in March tied to geopolitical tensions—with anticipated inflows of $40B to $50B this year. Spreads remain near historic lows, yet investor appetite shows few signs of weakening, the strategist said.

African (AFK) sovereigns have emerged as standout performers, with Nigeria and Angola drawing increased attention as investors seek alternatives to traditional Middle Eastern oil exporters, Weiler noted. At the same time, many emerging market governments are diversifying their funding strategies by issuing more debt in local and niche currencies to reduce exposure to U.S. dollar (DXY) volatility.

Macro dynamics may provide an additional tailwind. According to J.P. Morgan Asset Management, if the Federal Reserve continues to hold rates steady while other central banks tighten, narrowing short-term yield differentials could strengthen foreign currencies against the dollar—a potential boost for international equities and emerging market assets alike.

data.title: Iran war costs reach $38B as inflation, supply risks mount
data.description:
The war with Iran cost U.S. taxpayers about $38 billion during its first five months and is expected to add to inflation, according to a new Congressional Budget Office analysis.

The estimate covers replacement weapons, equipment lost in combat, additional flight operations and higher fuel expenses. It is close to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s July estimate of $37.5 billion.

The CBO said the conflict could cost another $2 billion to $3 billion for each additional month. Expenses could rise faster if fighting intensifies.

For investors, the report points to continued demand for defense equipment while raising concerns about interest rates and consumer spending. Higher energy costs could keep inflation above the Federal Reserve’s preferred path, potentially delaying rate cuts. Defense contractors may benefit from efforts to replenish weapons stockpiles, though federal funding remains subject to congressional approval.

Inflation pressure builds

Disruptions to oil and gas shipments through the Strait of Hormuz are expected to lift a key inflation gauge by about half a percentage point in early 2027 compared with the CBO’s February forecast.

Core personal consumption expenditures inflation, which excludes food and energy, is projected to be 0.3 percentage point higher. The CBO expects those underlying price pressures to emerge more slowly but persist longer.

That outlook could complicate the Federal Reserve’s policy decisions. A sustained increase in core inflation may reduce the central bank’s flexibility to lower interest rates even if economic growth weakens.

Weapons inventories face lengthy recovery

The fighting has also reduced U.S. munitions inventories. Rebuilding some stockpiles could take five years or more, according to the CBO.

The shortage may limit the military’s ability to respond to another large conflict, particularly one involving extensive use of ballistic and cruise missiles. The report identified a potential China-Taiwan conflict as one scenario in which those constraints could become significant.

A separate assessment by the Pentagon’s inspector general reportedly found that the defense industry cannot currently replace munitions as quickly as they are being consumed.

Trump has disputed concerns about shortages, saying the United States has ample ammunition.

Congress weighs additional funding

House Republicans advanced a budget plan in July that would provide $73 billion to the military and intelligence agencies for Iran-related expenses. The proposal has stalled in the Senate and may not receive consideration until after the Nov. 3 midterm elections.

Lawmakers are also considering a separate $350 billion increase in mandatory Pentagon spending. Part of that package would be financed through efforts to reduce healthcare fraud.

The two proposals could be combined after the election. Trump, who said in March that the conflict was nearly finished, has since acknowledged that it could continue beyond Election Day.

data.title: Autodesk initiated with Neutral rating due to near-term AI concerns: Cantor
data.description:
Cantor initiated coverage on Autodesk (ADSK) with a Neutral rating, as the financial services firm believes the rise of artificial intelligence poses a credible threat to the design software stalwart.

"ADSK is the global leader in Design software, with strong franchises in AutoCAD, Revit, Fusion, Civil 3D, Inventor, and Forma," said Cantor analyst Mason Marion in an in-depth investor report. "While AI poses perhaps the most credible threat to these franchises in ADSK's history, we expect the company to endure and grow in the AI era."

"ADSK is not standing by idly, investing in proprietary 3D generative AI models (neural CAD) and infusing Autodesk AI throughout its platform," he added. "Outside of Design, ADSK is leveraging its strong Design franchises to expand into Construction with Forma for Construction ($600m+ TTM rev growing 20%+)."

In addition, Autodesk's recent $3.6B acquisition of MaintainX is expected to increase its total addressable market.

Cantor set a price target of $215 on Autodesk, as it believes the market has already established a fair value for the stock.
